four_lom_index_recovered.first_attempt_failed_because: The pulse generator had no way to append a trailing button, so it overwrote the confirm press in the source script and player one never joined. The generator now takes --then.

SCREEN_NAMING.why_this_note: The two setup screens are easy to mislabel, and were. The screen TITLED "Arena Mode Select" is functionally the CONNECTION chooser - how do you connect - while the screen titled "Game Settings" is where the match MODE is actually chosen. Corrected after the capture files were named the wrong way round.

connection_screen.purpose: choose how to connect: Host Multi-Card Game, Host Single-Card Game, Join Wireless Game, Exit

mode_select_screen.purpose: choose the arena, the match mode (Deathmatch or Capture) and the time limit, then Start Game

in_match_hud.purpose: the bottom-screen HUD during a match - radar, player slots, action buttons

SCREEN_NAMING.note: The config keys below remain arena_mode_select and game_settings because those are the game s own titles and the entries under each are content-correct. Only the capture FILENAMES were wrong.

CHANNEL_ORDER_CORRECTION.what_went_wrong: melonDS writes its framebuffer as BGRA. Every screen capture was read as RGBA, so red and blue were exchanged in every colour measured from a captured frame.
CHANNEL_ORDER_CORRECTION.reported_by: Visual review: the menu shots looked colour-inverted.
CHANNEL_ORDER_CORRECTION.the_worst_part: The port ALREADY had a gold title and blue items, and they were essentially right. They were overwritten with the swapped values, and test_runtime.gd - which had correctly been asserting gold and blue - was edited to assert the swapped ones. A test that was catching the error was changed to endorse it.
CHANNEL_ORDER_CORRECTION.fixed: ds_menu.gd, test_runtime.gd and test_menu_strings.gd all restored to the corrected measurements, and every .bin capture reconverted to PNG with the right channel order.
CHANNEL_ORDER_CORRECTION.standing_rule: Any colour taken from a melonDS framebuffer must be read BGRA. Geometry measurements are unaffected - only colour was wrong.

SIDE_BY_SIDE_COMPARISON.ds: out/work/menu_shots/mode_select_screen.png (Game Settings, captured from the running game)
what_matches: Gold title, blue entries - the palette is right now that the BGRA order is fixed.
The four connection strings are exact: Host Multi-Card Game, Host Single-Card Game, Join Wireless Game, Exit.
what_does_NOT_match: TITLE: the port says "Arena Setup". The DS says "Game Settings". The port title is invented.
LAYOUT: the DS centres each VALUE with a left and right arrow flanking it. The port uses a two-column label-left / value-right list with no arrows. Completely different presentation.
ROW COUNT: the DS Game Settings screen has exactly THREE rows - arena, mode, time. The port shows seven: Map, Game Mode, Characters, Character, Balance, Modifier, Time Limit.
MISSING ACTION: the DS has Start Game in cyan at the bottom. The port has no Start Game at all.
SCREEN MERGING: the DS keeps connection choices on a SEPARATE screen titled Arena Mode Select. The port lists Host/Join/Exit inline underneath the settings, merging two screens into one.
ENHANCEMENTS INLINE: Characters, Balance, Modifier and Score Limit are port additions shown among the real rows with nothing distinguishing them.
SIDE_BY_SIDE_COMPARISON.assessment: The strings and the palette are right; the STRUCTURE is not. Menu parity had been scored on vocabulary, colour and measured geometry without ever rendering the port and looking. That was too generous.
SIDE_BY_SIDE_COMPARISON.parity_correction: Menus dropped from 96 to 55. The decoded data is sound - what was missing is that the port does not yet USE the decoded structure, only the decoded words.

Add Start Game as a cyan action at y 164-174.

Move the enhancement rows behind the existing show_enhancements flag so they cannot be mistaken for parity.

RENDER_SCALING_FIX.reported_by: Visual review - starfield smudgy and texture-filtered, UI scaling and alignment wrong.
RENDER_SCALING_FIX.root_cause: project.godot had window/stretch/mode="canvas_items". The viewport was declared 256x192 but every widget was actually DRAWN at the 1024x768 window size and scaled smoothly. Text and the starfield were filtered, and no measured DS coordinate could line up because nothing was rendering in DS pixels.
RENDER_SCALING_FIX.fix: window/stretch/mode="viewport" plus window/stretch/scale_mode="integer". The frame is drawn at 256x192 and the result is scaled by a whole number, so one DS pixel is always a square block.
RENDER_SCALING_FIX.second_fault: REFERENCE_PITCH 28 was being applied to the settings screen. That is the Arena Mode Select value. Game Settings uses 40 - rows at y 35, 75, 115. Added OPTION_PITCH 40 with a per-screen flag.
RENDER_SCALING_FIX.result: The port now renders 256x192 native with the three option rows correctly spaced.
still_wrong: Start Game sits bottom-LEFT and blue. The DS centres it at y 164-174 in cyan.

The starfield draws as streaks rather than discrete points - it still looks nothing like the DS field of single white pixels. starfield.gd also still runs on a 60Hz assumption while the simulation is 30Hz.
Arena Mode Select is still not a separate screen.
RENDER_SCALING_FIX.lesson: Every measured DS coordinate was useless while the renderer was not in DS pixels. This should have been checked before any layout measurement was applied to the port.

font_settled: The font entry has come off this list. It asked for 'glyph shapes and per-character advances, needed for exact text placement', and both are exported: tools/export_custom_fonts.py decodes the 4bpp archive assets and writes build/assets/fonts/font_18.lsw2font, which carries an atlas plus a per-glyph advance, and that font was matched to six row widths read out of a live pause menu with total error zero. port/frontend/gamefont.cpp reads it and lsw2_font_width sums the advances the way the game does.
